html:
The Military Frontier was a border zone that the Habsburgs ran directly as an army district along their frontier with the Ottoman Empire, from the 1550s until 1881. Its core lay in Croatia, with Karlovac, founded in 1579, as a main fortress.

Settlers, many of them Orthodox Vlachs and Serbs fleeing Ottoman lands, got land and freedom from serfdom in return for lifelong military service. The frontier kept the Ottomans out but cut a broad belt of Croatia off from the rule of the Croatian ban and diet. Its Serb communities remained in places like the Krajina, which made them central to the war of the 1990s. The zone was joined back to Croatia in 1881.
